items.name: SplashPasto Paint
items.description:
SplashPasto Paint — A LoRA for Color, Emotion, and Texture

The SplashPasto Paint LoRA brings a vivid painterly life to your generations, transforming any subject into a world of expressive color, emotion, and textured depth. Built to evoke the lush vibrancy of impressionism and the bold physicality of impasto, this LoRA specializes in fusing modern fantasy, sci-fi, and artistic emotion through brushstroke-like expression. Use the keyword SplashPastoDaal to activate its full effect.

About the Style

SplashPasto Paint interprets your prompts with a focus on color harmony, emotional resonance, and tactile texture. It thrives on visible brush movement, layered pigment, and paint-like abstraction while keeping subjects recognizable and emotionally charged. Faces gain emotional nuance through hue and lighting, landscapes pulse with energy, and machinery or architecture gleam with sculpted pigment. The model beautifully balances expressive motion and structured form.

Usage Tips

• Works best at weights between 0.5 – 1.5, with the sweet spot around 1.0 for strong stylistic adherence.
• Lower strengths (0.5–0.8): More photographic or natural appearance, with subtle painterly influence.
• Higher strengths (1.2–1.5): Pushes the scene toward expressive abstraction, bold color, and energetic texture.
• Performs consistently well across people, animals, places, and objects.
• Avoid prompts for “realistic photography”—instead, use descriptive, emotive, and painterly language to maximize effect.
• Adding notes like “thick impasto on foreground”, “bright color diffusion in light areas”, or “brush texture emphasized in emotion zones” helps guide where texture intensity is desired.

Ideal For

  • Expressive fantasy portraits

  • Sci-fi emotion studies

  • Mythical and surreal worlds

  • Painterly animal scenes

  • Textured environment art

Share the Vibe

If SplashPasto Paint inspires you, give it a thumbs up and post your first image on the LoRA page! Seeing your creations helps fuel future updates and keeps this project alive with community energy. Let’s fill the feed with color, emotion, and the texture of imagination.

items.name: Splashing With Foot / Liquid Drip
items.description:
This LoRA is designed to help models (checkpoints) draw the correct splash. Without it, models do not draw splashes from a leg raised in the air, but from one that is submerged in water.

Prompt examples:

1girl, solo, from side, sitting, soaking feet, leg up, splashing, water, swimsuit
1boy, solo, from side, standing on one leg, knee up, wading, blood drip, blood, casual
1girl, solo, from behind, walking on liquid, wading, gradient water, blue water, yellow water, dress

Activation tags:

splashing

or

<liquid name> splashing

like lava splashing.

or

<liquid name> drip

like honey drip.

If the LoRA's effect is too strong (for example, the character does not want to change a pose to specified), then reduce LoRA strength.

Examples of liquids:

  • acid

  • blood

  • chocolate

  • honey

  • lava

  • milk

  • motor oil

  • and many more.

It may be necessary to add water to the negatives.

Also this LoRA is trained to understand the color of water:

  • purple water

  • black water

  • yellow water

  • gradient water, red water, blue water

  • etc.

Useful tags:

  • foot out of frame – analogue of "cowboy shot" for a sitting persons

  • feet out of frame – same with both feet down

  • soaking feet

  • wading

  • standing on one leg

  • walking

  • leg up

  • leg lift

  • foot up

  • knee up

  • kicking

  • high kick

  • outstretched leg

  • plantar flexion

  • motion lines

  • motion blur

You can control the camera with default tags:

  • foot focus

  • straight-on - may not work well

  • from side

  • from behind

  • from above

  • from below

  • perspective

  • etc.

as well as their combinations: "from side, from above, perspective".

items.name: Glitch art_splash paint
items.description:
Lora is multi-tagged, so you don't have to use all the trigger words at once. You can create images with splattered paint or just glitch art. The monochromatic tag keeps the main image within a single color (this doesn't affect the color of glitches and paint splatters, but their color can also be controlled via Prompt). And, of course, you can control the strength of each trigger. Overall, this isn't just a Lora style mimicking certain styles and subgenres, but a fairly flexible tool.

strength 0.7-1.5

Instead of results

SDXL Ilustrios is still unrivaled in terms of creating stylistic adapters, flexibility, and ease of inference. Especially when it comes to local generation. It's still my favorite, and other models will have a long way to go to catch up. Some custom checkpoints are on a completely different level compared to the initial tunes or new models when it comes to anime generation. And this model actually reflects that.

zimage (z-anime) I'd call it a candidate to replace lustrios – in some distant future. It has its own vibe, its own charm, but its negative prompt handling is terrible. And the lack of training data is taking its toll. Although I probably should have used a non-distilled model. It should work better with Lors. Maybe I'll tune it someday.

Anima - although I used the preview 3 model for training and generation, not the release version (I don't think this makes much of a difference, judging by the sample images of the release version). The model is new and therefore rather clumsy. It seems to lean toward pop art and retro art. I don't understand the hype around it, to be honest. It's too monotonous and cheap-looking by default, and when using it, I can't shake the feeling that it's significantly behind what's already out there, at least a year or more (barring a miracle). Currently, it's a good competitor and replacement for SD 1.5, but nothing more. There are some indications that it won't surpass that ceiling. However, it's possible that Anima 2 or Anima 3 will be much better. The developers still have the dataset. And labeled data is already 70% of the new model on any architecture.

However, this LoRa, in my opinion, turned out quite good, and overall, the model trains better than I expected. Although it's difficult to judge with only one trained Lora. I still have the training tools on the PC, so I might train something else. Otherwise, I don't see this model as promising in the near future. That's my current opinion.

items.name: Gacha splash LORA
items.description:
The training dataset is 100% generated by NovelAI. No real artwork is used.

Checkout my Alter version, which uses real artwork: https://civitai.com/models/85859/gacha-splash-alter

3.0 version is released. I rebuilt the entire training set for this version.

Notes:

  1. Use hires fix + SD upscale or MultiDiffusion to get better face details.

  2. Try adding wood, stone in negative prompt if you see too many woods, stones, structures. You may also emphasize it. For example, the bottle keeps getting transformed into structures till I add wood, stone.

A 2.0 version is released:

A gacha splash style lora. Make sure you start with the following template and add your background prompts.

[(white background:1.5)::5], isometric OR hexagon , 1 girl, mid shot, full body, <add your background prompts here>

Suggested resolution: 640X640 with hires fix. You may modify your prompt and resolution after successfully getting the effect.

I trained two different versions with different learning rate and scheduler.

Gacha Splash Fantasy fits more in abstract backgrounds.

Gacha Splash is intentionally trained to be slightly overfit. It fits greatly for architectures.

See compares from sample images

Notes:

1. If your characters are always wearing jackets/half off jackets, try adding "off shoulder" in negative prompt. You may further add "jackets"/ "bare shoulders" if the issue persists.

2. Similar as the jacket issue, if you find any elements that are always being generated, try adding them into negative prompt first. The training dataset is well tagged. Therefore AI should be able to remove these elements.

Prompts like hexagon and isometric help to shape the gacha splash effect. There are some alternative choices.

items.name: Gacha Splash Alter
items.description:
Introducing a better way to use this LoRA with refiner. All sample images are generated in this way:

Settings:

  1. Check "Hires fix: show hires checkpoint and sampler selection".

  2. Set "Hires fix: which pass to enable refiner for" to first pass".

  3. Merge LoRA into your base model. Recommend SilvermoonxMix Base mode. Here is a merged version: https://civitai.com/models/54152?modelVersionId=282796

Instruction:

  1. Set base checkpoint to the merged one in Settings#3.

  2. Set Hires, refiner, ADetailer (optional) checkpoint to the one with your desired style (For example, pastel mix)

  3. Suggested configurations:
    DPM++ SDE Karras
    Sampling steps 28

    Refiner switch at 0.425

基于refiner的模型使用手法 https://www.bilibili.com/video/BV1rN4y1B7eg/

前期设置：

  • 在设置中开启高清修复模型选择

  • 在设置中把refiner改为first pass,这样确保在高清修复的过程中不使用refiner

  • 把立绘法LoRA融进你的基础模型中，或者直接使用融合了立绘法LoRA的银月Mix: https://civitai.com/models/54152?modelVersionId=282796

  • 融合插件推荐使用: SuperMergage https://github.com/hako-mikan/sd-webui-supermerger

  • （可选）推荐使用ADetailer插件增加面部细节：https://github.com/Bing-su/adetailer

使用设置：

  1. 把基础模型设置为融合了立绘法LoRA的模型

  2. 把高清修复和Refiner模型设置为你想用的风格化模型

  3. 根据我的测试，SDE采样器，迭代步数28，refiner切入时机设置为0.425

  4. 如果你使用了ADetailer插件，把ADetailer的inpaint模型也改成同样的风格化模型

不同的模型需要不同的white background权重。如果没有立绘效果，请适当加权。

Different models need different weights of "white background" to get the effect. Increase the weight as you need.

Sample images were generated by https://civitai.com/models/54152/silvermoonmix-base-model

Check my profile for more LoRAs https://civitai.com/user/silvermoong/models
